rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lead-in for {{prompt:ae101-m5-done-done}} is two sentences and does not open 'Ask Claude to…', unlike every other {{prompt:}} lead-in in the corpus (grepped ~15 instances, all 'Ask/Tell Claude to X'). Evaluated against §2a's own diagnostic ('does the lead-in tell the student something they will not have absorbed by the time they finish reading the fence?'): the fence itself ('Are we done-done? By done-done I mean: 1)…4)…') is fully self-explanatory as a semantic summary, so a generic 'Ask Claude whether it's done-done' restatement would be the exact low-value duplication §2a warns against. The two sentences instead carry session-boundary information the fence cannot ('runs in the session you sent off', not a fresh session) which is load-bearing per §40's session-boundary check. Kept as a deliberate departure, not a violation.
